title: What is known about 1RB1LC_1LC1RD_1LA0LB_0RB1RE_1RF0RA_---0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LC_1LC1RD_1LA0LB_0RB1RE_1RF0RA_---0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is mostly two blocks: an alternating block (10)^x followed by a solid block 1^y. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) finds no halt in the first 1015 steps.

What Lean proves. The whole frame map: 6 tape shapes, 30 cases, each proved for all sizes by a symbolic run (next_sound), and the cases where the map is undefined halt (none_halts). So the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the map, iterated from the frame the run reaches after 1 steps, reaches one of those cases (halts_iff). By native_decide the first 108 frames (about 5.95·1011 machine steps) do not. Whether the orbit ever does is open.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,959 cells have been visited and 2,754 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.333). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.326).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) runs 1015 steps without a halt. The macro simulator cuts the tape into blocks of K cells, run-length codes them, and crosses a whole run at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with; it agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun cell for cell.

claims.title: Doubling at the left end
claims.text: At the moments the head reaches a new cell on the left between steps 9.85·107 and 9.99·107, the tape is (10)^x 1^y with x = 85, 173, 349, 701 and y falling by the same amounts.

claims.title: The halting state, seen from the run
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps state F was entered 30,382 times, always reading a 1 (F0 halts).

claims.title: The frame map agrees with the machine on a grid
claims.text: For each of the 6 frames and every canonical choice of sizes below 20, the machine reaches exactly the frame, sizes and step count the fitted map predicts (31,259 frames, py/framemap.py verify 20). The map is now proved in Lean; this check is how it was found.

claims.title: The frame map agrees with the run
claims.text: Run from blank tape next to the machine, the fitted map predicts the whole tape at each of the 41,118 frames in the first 5·106 steps (py/framemap.py real 5000000).

claims.title: The whole frame map
claims.text: next in lean/Phases.lean sends each of the 6 frames to the next one the machine reaches, in 30 cases; next_sound proves every case for all parameters, each from a symbolic run in lean/Pieces.lean (generated by py/pieces.py) glued by tape_eq. Where next is undefined (.b l j 2, .d l 0 1, .d l 1 0) the machine halts (none_halts).

claims.title: Halts if and only if the map reaches an undefined case
claims.text: init_start: the run from blank tape reaches Ph.e 1 0 after 1 steps. halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of next from there is a frame where next is none.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> frames
claims.text: no_halt_phases, by native_decide: the first 108 iterates are defined. By the step counts of the fitted map (py/framemap.py run 100000000) that is about 5.95·1011 machine steps.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Its tape is an alternating block followed by a solid block; at the left end the alternating block about doubles again and again, eating into the solid block, until the solid block is used up and a new round starts.

facts.text: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> frames of the frame map proved in Lean (about 5.95·10<sup>11</sup> machine steps).
It halts if and only if the frame map, iterated from the first frame, reaches a frame where it is undefined.
No halt in an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells).
The alternating block doubles at the expense of the solid block.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the C simulator; 3,959 cells visited.

sections.heading: What the machine does
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell on the left. With a for 10, around step 9.85·107:

Each time, the alternating block goes from x to 2x + 3 (85, 173, 349, 701) and the solid block loses the same number of cells (1663 − 173 = 1490, 1490 − 349 = 1141, 1141 − 701 = 440). Rewriting a block of length x costs about x passes of length x, so the step count between left growths grows like the square of the width (61,683, 247,275 and 990,171 steps here), and the width grows like the cube root of the step count. When the solid block runs out a new round starts. This is the same doubling seen in the three machines 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_…_1RF0LD_---0RE, with different states.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The halting transition is F reading a 0. F is entered only from E reading a 0 (1RF), so a halt needs E>0 0: E on a 0 with another 0 just to its right. In the first 108 steps F was entered 30,382 times, every time on a 1, and 30,101 of those times at least 7 cells from the left end.

Whether the end of a round can leave E in front of two 0s is open. In the related machines 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_…_1RF0LD_---0RE the halt can only come at the moment the tape is all 1s, and only for a sparse list of tape lengths; whether the same holds here has not been checked.

sections.heading: The frame map in Lean
html: The frames (blank tape outside; X is the head in state X on the next cell; u^v is v copies of u, so 11^L is 2L ones; a frame counts only at a moment where the head turns round):

• b: 1^L B 10 10^j 1^R
  • a: 1^L 10^j 110 A 1^R
  • c: 1^L 0 C 0 10^j 1^R
  • d: 1^L A 01 10^j 1^R
  • e: 1^L 10^j B
  • f: 1^L 10^j 1101 B
The map next (Lean names; each variable a natural number):

The map was found by fitting the machine's runs (py/framemap.py) and collapsing the fit into cases (py/pieces.py); Lean then checks every case for all sizes. It is undefined only at .b l j 2, .d l 0 1, .d l 1 0, and those halt. So the open question is exactly whether the orbit of Ph.e 1 0 reaches one of them; the first 108 frames do not.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.333). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.326).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,959 cells (1,403 left of the start, 1,816 right), with a density of 1s of 0.696.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.
